A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GoRank/GoTrim work and contain complete main text and Appendices A–L. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite repagination and two rerendered panels.

before.justification: v7 reports original ranking and robust mean-estimation experiments on synthetic data and Basel temperature measurements in Sections 3.2 and 4.3, with additional experimental results in the appendices.

after.justification: v8 retains these original experiments, including results on different graph topologies, asynchronous ranking, larger networks, and sparse graphs.

M1.justification: The GoRank, GoTrim, Baseline++, and asynchronous GoRank procedures are unchanged. Algorithm 1 changes the comment update(k,t) to update(k,s), matching the existing loop variable without changing the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic data and Basel Luftklima measurements for ranking and trimmed mean estimation. Graph families, contamination scenarios, and synchronous/asynchronous coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain Chiuso et al.'s Baseline and Baseline++ for ranking, and the same GoTrim combinations, ClippedGossip from He et al., and corrupted-mean reference for mean estimation. The asynchronous comparison also retains its comparator set.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, graph construction, contamination settings, error metrics, and iteration budgets are unchanged in Sections 3.2 and 4.3 and Appendices G–K. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The rank-centrality and weight-bound checks, graph-connectivity analyses, and clustered/sparse-network robustness studies are retained. No ablation, sensitivity analysis, or robustness case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 3.2 retains 1,000 trials for the rank-dependent analysis and means and standard deviations from 100 trials for convergence comparisons. Repeated-run and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical values, comparative trends, and findings are retained across the main text and appendices. Visual comparison confirms that the rerendered Figures 8(c) and 9(c) preserve the same curves and results.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, Theorems 1–4, and supporting derivations and proofs in Appendices B–F are unchanged. The new citation to asynchronous theory does not add a formal result or proof to this PDF.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: decentralized rank and trimmed mean estimation, convergence guarantees, breakdown-point analysis, and empirical effectiveness on contaminated data and poorly connected graphs.

C2.justification: Section 5 changes asynchronous theoretical analysis from planned future work to analysis attributed to a cited extension. Appendix H still retains the future-work wording. Other interpretations, applicability boundaries, and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v7 promises future public availability and points to supplementary material for code and data. v8 states public availability and supplies a specific repository address for the code and Basel dataset in Sections 3.2 and 4.3. Implementation and computing-resource details are unchanged.

R1.justification: v8 adds reference [35], Van Elst, Colin, and Clémençon's Asynchronous gossip algorithms for rank-based statistical methods, and cites it in Section 5. Remaining citation changes concern formatting or renumbering, without broader repositioning.

P1.justification: Limited edits correct an algorithm comment, standardize cross-references, revise availability and follow-up statements, expand acknowledgments, and replace the preprint footer with the NeurIPS 2025 notice. Section ordering and the overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 8(c) and 9(c) are replaced by raster renderings with lighter typography while preserving their content. First-page text and references undergo limited reflow and repagination; all figures and tables remain.

improvement.justification: Replacing v7's future-release statement and generic supplementary-material pointers with a concrete code/data repository address improves reproducibility documentation. The asynchronous follow-up citation adds useful context, although Appendix H retains inconsistent future-work wording. These are limited gains; the methods, scientific evidence, and proofs are unchanged.
